source_pins.benchmark_evaluation_status: CarBench is the reference surface-pressure benchmark for this dataset. Its evaluation code and models are not yet public (the repository currently publishes the benchmark description only); the official split files will also be mirrored there after the CarBench release. CarBench reports equal-point (unweighted) relative L2 under three evaluation protocols, compared in Elrefaie et al. (journal revision) on a stratified 61-geometry subset of the held-out test split. 'Subsampled' scores a 10,000-point prediction on those same 10,000 points. 'Interpolated' upscales that 10,000-point prediction to every native node by radial-basis interpolation; in that study its degradation relative to subsampled is dominated by interpolation error rather than by resolution. 'Patchwise' predicts every native node directly (ceil(N/1e4) disjoint 10,000-point passes, or a single geometry encoding with chunked queries for models such as AB-UPT and TripNet that decode arbitrary query points); its relative L2 tracks the subsampled values closely and preserves the model ordering. These labels describe how CarBench produced its published numbers and do not by themselves decide eligibility here. Eligibility follows the repository submission rules: a submission must supply one prediction for every native point of all 1,154 official_test cases and report every prescribed metric, including the area-weighted primary and the equal-point diagnostic. Any interpolation, mapping or resampling used to reach those native points is permitted, must be declared in discretization.json, and carries its own error into the score. No published CarBench value is usable as an official row as it stands: the protocol comparison covers 61 geometries rather than the 1,154-case official_test split, and its values are equal-point only, so they correspond to this dataset's surface_pressure_equal_entity_rel_l2 diagnostic rather than to the area-weighted primary metric. AB-UPT is evaluated from an author-provided checkpoint rather than a CarBench-trained model.

candidate_migration_notes: The closed schema-v3 candidate removes the legacy diagnostic volume_velocity_physical_rel_l2 and volume_pressure_physical_rel_l2 requirements. The native Table-5 evaluator has never published or consumed volume dual-volume support; its frozen primary contract is equal valid native nodes. This candidate migration is not an activated public scoring change because submissions remain closed and unapproved.

Relative field metrics are bound to the frozen Table-5 nondimensional targets, while the existing paper-compatible MAE/RMSE metrics remain dimensional. A candidate aggregate must emit and audit both bases from the same per-case inference stream.

The closed candidate replaces the stale prototype 16-station velocity panel with the five frozen Table-5 stations B.2, B.3, C.1, C.2, and C.3. Velocity profiles use physical polyline arc length and within-station centering; Cp retains exact rows A-J with physical connected-cut arc length and independently centered connected graphs. This is not an activated public profile-contract change while submissions remain closed.

scoring_support.closed_reason: Every contract input is frozen and every support artefact is generated and hash-pinned; opening submissions is a release decision for the dataset owner.

profile_support.note: One support file per scored test case, each pinning the native entity IDs the profile series are read at. Every case reports exactly 8 containment fallbacks: the eight vertical stations each begin at y = 0 on the ground plane, outside the fluid mesh.

public_source.note: The aggregate tables and the official split manifest enumerate 355 design variants, but run_350..run_354 have no per-run payload in the public release and are therefore unscoreable.

coverage_contract.public_ground_truth: Ground-truth fields are in the public dataset release.

public_supports.units_note: cpavg and the cfxavg/cfyavg/cfzavg skin-friction components are dimensionless coefficients.
public_supports.physical_weight_note: The published per-point dual areas are canonical. The dataset README warns that recomputing polygon areas with VTK can drift for non-planar quads, so they must not be regenerated.

v1 scores the volume with equal-cell weighting. WindsorML publishes no cell-volume sidecar and generating one for ~291M cells x 350 cases costs roughly 400 GB and 1,000 CPU-hours, so the cell-volume-weighted variants are deferred.

force_convention.axes_note: The vertical axis is +y. The body sits on a ground plane at y=0 spanning y in [0, 0.343] and is laterally symmetric about z=0. Mapping lift to +z collapses cl from about 0.49 to about -0.01.
force_convention.audit_note: Truth and prediction are integrated identically so a perfect prediction scores R^2 = 1; the published CSV bounds the truth integration rather than defining it.

relative_l2_policy.vector_assembly_note: Vector components are published as independent scalar arrays. Relative L2 recombines exactly from per-component squared sums; Euclidean MAE and RMSE do not, and are reported per component.

scored_case_set.excluded_reason: The official manifest assigns 355 identifiers, but run_350 through run_354 have no per-run payload in the public release. run_352 (high_drag) and run_354 (baseline and low_drag test sets) are therefore unscoreable.
scored_case_set.comparability_note: Scores on these case sets are not comparable to any evaluation run against the unreduced official manifest.

component_weights.rationale: Identical to AhmedML and HiLiftAeroML component for component, and to DrivAerML apart from its force group, which splits three ways (cd 0.15, cl 0.05, c_pitch 0.05) because it scores pitching moment. WindsorML publishes cmy, so a c_pitch_r2 term is supported by the data, but it would need surface moment integration and a pinned moment reference point that the dataset does not publish. Not adopted.
